examples.ko: 저는 이번 시험을 잘 볼 수 있다고 자신해요.
examples.en: I'm confident I can do well on this exam.
He was confident in his own ability.
If you're too sure of yourself, you might slip up.

examples.ko: 팀장님은 이 계획이 성공할 거라고 자신하세요.
examples.en: The team leader is confident this plan will succeed.
It was cool how confident he was about winning.

examples.ko: 그렇게 자신하지 말고 한 번 더 확인해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't be so sure; check one more time.

explain: '자신 있다'는 일상에서 더 자주 써요. '자신하다'는 '~다고 자신하다'처럼 장담하는 느낌이 강하고, 말이나 글에서 더 딱딱해요. 너무 크게 장담하면 '자만하다'로 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: '자신 있다' is more common in daily talk. '자신하다' sounds like making a bold claim, usually in the pattern '~다고 자신하다', and is a bit formal. If you overdo it, it can sound like '자만하다' (be conceited).

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어려도 약아서 손해 보는 일이 없어요.
examples.en: That kid is young but shrewd and never loses out.
If you act calculating, your friends won't like it.

examples.ko: 동생은 약아요. 심부름은 늘 저한테 시켜요.
examples.en: My younger brother is sly. He always makes me run the errands.
A shrewd person looks after their own interests first.

examples.ko: 그 가게 주인은 약아서 속기 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: The shop owner is sharp, so it's hard to trick him.

examples.ko: 너무 약아 보이는 사람은 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to trust someone who looks too calculating.

explain: '똑똑하다'는 머리가 좋다는 칭찬이고, '약다'는 자기 이익을 잘 챙기는 영리함이라 칭찬이 아닐 때가 많아요. '영악하다', '꾀바르다'와 비슷하지만 '약다'가 더 가볍고 일상적이에요.
explain_en: '똑똑하다' praises intelligence, while '약다' means being clever at protecting your own interest, so it is often not a compliment. It is close to '영악하다' and '꾀바르다' but lighter and more everyday.

examples.en: When a child recognizes danger, he stops right away.
By the time I noticed the problem, it was already too late.
People perceive color first.

examples.ko: 자신의 감정을 인지하는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to be aware of your own feelings.

examples.ko: 회사는 사고 사실을 인지하고 조사를 시작했어요.
examples.en: The company became aware of the accident and began an investigation.
I wasn't aware of that rule.

explain: '알다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 뉴스나 보고서에서 '문제를 인지하다'처럼 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '알아차리다', '깨닫다'가 더 자연스러워요. '인식하다'와 비슷한데, '인지하다'는 어떤 사실이 있다는 걸 아는 쪽이에요.
explain_en: A stiffer word than '알다', common in news and reports (e.g. '문제를 인지하다'). In daily talk, '알아차리다' or '깨닫다' sounds more natural. It is close to '인식하다', but '인지하다' stresses becoming aware that something exists.

examples.ko: 선생님은 새 단어를 일상생활과 관련시켜 가르쳐 주세요.
examples.en: The teacher teaches new words by relating them to daily life.

examples.ko: 이 사건을 그 사람과 관련시키지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't connect this incident to that person.
I thought about the two things together.
If you link a memory to a place, it lasts longer.

examples.ko: 저는 그 일을 제 문제와 관련시켰어요.
examples.en: I connected that matter to my own problem.
The news is linking the two incidents.

explain: '관련되다'는 저절로 연결된 상태이고, '관련시키다'는 누군가 일부러 연결한다는 차이가 있어요. '연결하다'는 물건이나 선에도 쓰지만 '관련시키다'는 일이나 생각을 이을 때 써요. '~을 ~와 관련시키다' 틀로 써요.
explain_en: '관련되다' is a state of being linked on its own, while '관련시키다' means someone links things on purpose. '연결하다' also works for objects and lines, but '관련시키다' is used for events and ideas. The pattern is '~을 ~와 관련시키다'.

examples.ko: 이 책에는 옛날 생활이 자세히 기술돼 있어요.
examples.en: Life in the old days is described in detail in this book.
The cause of the accident was described like this in the report.

examples.ko: 그 방법은 설명서 마지막에 기술될 거예요.
examples.en: That method will be described at the end of the manual.
The content described differs from the facts.

examples.ko: 논문에는 실험 과정이 순서대로 기술되어야 해요.
examples.en: In a paper, the experiment steps must be described in order.

examples.ko: 역사 속 인물은 책마다 다르게 기술돼요.
examples.en: Historical figures are described differently in each book.

explain: '쓰여 있다'보다 딱딱한 글말이에요. 논문·보고서·설명서에서 '~에 기술되어 있다'로 많이 써요. 말할 때는 '나와 있어요', '쓰여 있어요'가 자연스러워요. 능동형은 '기술하다'예요.
explain_en: A stiffer written word than '쓰여 있다', used in papers, reports and manuals as '~에 기술되어 있다'. In speech, '나와 있어요' or '쓰여 있어요' is more natural. The active form is '기술하다'.

examples.ko: 이 글은 그날의 모습을 자세히 기술해요.
examples.en: This text describes that day's scene in detail.
I wrote up the experiment results in the report.

examples.ko: 사건을 있는 그대로 기술하는 것이 중요해요.
examples.en: It's important to describe the event just as it was.
Please describe the problem in the box below.

examples.ko: 저자는 한국의 역사를 짧게 기술하고 있어요.
examples.en: The author describes Korean history briefly.
Describing what you saw is harder than you'd think.

explain: '설명하다'는 상대에게 이해시키려고 말하는 것이고, '기술하다'는 있는 사실을 글로 적는다는 느낌이 강해요. 신청서나 설문의 '기술해 주세요'에서 자주 만나요. 같은 소리의 '기술(技術, skill)'과 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: '설명하다' is explaining so someone understands; '기술하다' leans toward writing down facts as they are. You often meet it on forms: '기술해 주세요'. Don't confuse it with '기술' meaning skill.

examples.ko: 이 대회 결과는 역사에 기록될 거예요.
examples.en: This tournament's result will go down in history.
Every conversation is recorded on the computer.
The highest temperature was recorded that day.
The recorded time isn't accurate.
His name is recorded in the book.

examples.ko: 내 이름이 명단에 기록되는 순간을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the moment my name was recorded on the list.

explain: '기록되다'는 어떤 내용이 글이나 자료로 남는다는 뜻이에요. '적히다'는 글자로 쓰여 있다는 쪽이고, '기록되다'는 나중에 참고하려고 남겨 둔다는 느낌이 강해요. '신기록이 기록되다'처럼 같은 말이 겹치면 '신기록을 세우다'가 자연스러워요. 능동형은 '기록하다'예요.
explain_en: '기록되다' means content is kept as writing or data. '적히다' just means being written down, while '기록되다' feels like being kept for later reference. If the word repeats, as in '신기록이 기록되다', '신기록을 세우다' sounds more natural. The active form is '기록하다'.

examples.en: It rained, so the playground is muddy.
The ground was soggy and my shoes got soaked.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에는 길이 질어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: After rain the road is muddy, so be careful.
Rice that is too soft and wet doesn't taste good.

examples.ko: 반죽이 질게 되면 밀가루를 더 넣으세요.
examples.en: If the dough gets too wet, add more flour.

examples.ko: 오늘은 길이 질지 않아서 걷기 좋아요.
examples.en: The road isn't muddy today, so it's good for walking.

explain: '질다'는 땅이나 밥, 반죽에 물기가 너무 많을 때 써요. 반대는 '되다'(밥이 되다)예요. 'ㄹ' 받침 때문에 '진 길', '지니까'처럼 ㄹ이 빠져요. 사람에게 쓰는 말이 아니에요.
explain_en: '질다' describes ground, rice or dough that has too much moisture. The opposite is '되다' (as in rice being firm). Because the stem ends in ㄹ, the ㄹ drops: '진 길', '지니까'. It isn't used for people.

examples.en: If a problem occurs, please tell me right away.
A lot of noise is generated because of the construction.
An accident occurred on the road yesterday.
The company pays the costs that arise.
I'm looking for the reason errors occur.
When a fire breaks out, move calmly.

explain: 일상에서는 '발생하다'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '발생되다'는 '문제가 발생되다'처럼 쓰는데, '발생하다'로 충분한 말에 '되다'를 붙인 것이라 어색하다고 보는 사람도 있어요. 시험이나 글에서는 '발생하다'를 쓰면 안전해요.
explain_en: In daily use '발생하다' is far more common. '발생되다' (as in '문제가 발생되다') adds '되다' to a verb that already works on its own, so some people think it sounds off. In exams or writing, '발생하다' is the safe choice.

examples.en: A new air conditioner was installed in the classroom.

examples.ko: 이 건물 입구에는 카메라가 설치돼 있어요.
examples.en: Cameras are installed at the entrance of this building.
When the app is installed, an icon appears.
A traffic light will be installed in front of the crosswalk.
I want to delete the installed program.
With the elevator installed, it got more convenient.

explain: '설치하다'는 하는 사람이 중심이고, '설치되다'는 이미 달려 있는 결과 상태가 중심이에요. 기계·프로그램에 쓰고, 가구는 보통 '놓다'를 써요. 앱이나 프로그램은 '깔리다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '설치하다' focuses on the person doing it, '설치되다' on the resulting state. It is used for machines and programs; for furniture, people usually say '놓다'. '깔리다' is a more casual word for apps and programs.

examples.ko: 이 일을 제가 직접 말하기가 좀 무엇해요.
examples.en: It's a bit awkward for me to say this directly.
It's a bit awkward to call at this late hour.
It was awkward to refuse, so I just went.
It feels awkward to talk about money with a friend.
It's a bit awkward to be the one who contacts first.
If it's awkward, let's talk again next time.

explain: '말하기 무엇하다'처럼 하기 곤란하거나 어색한 걸 돌려 말할 때 써요. 말하는 사람이 일부러 말끝을 흐리는 느낌이에요. '곤란하다', '어색하다'보다 부드럽고, 주로 '~기가 무엇하다' 틀로 써요.
explain_en: Used to indirectly say something is awkward or hard to do, as in '말하기 무엇하다'. The speaker softens the sentence on purpose. It is gentler than '곤란하다' or '어색하다' and mostly appears in the pattern '~기가 무엇하다'.

examples.en: You need practice in thinking logically.
He is a person who thinks about problems differently.
If you think deeply, the answer shows up.
Children think while they play.
When I thought flexibly, a solution came to mind.
Gather information before you reason it through.

explain: '생각하다'는 일상 말이고, '사고하다'는 논리적으로 따져 생각한다는 딱딱한 글말이에요. 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 '사고력', '창의적으로 사고하다'처럼 교육·논문에서 자주 나와요. 소리가 같은 '사고(事故, accident)'와 구별하세요.
explain_en: '생각하다' is everyday; '사고하다' is a stiff written word for reasoning logically. It's rare in conversation and shows up in education and papers, like '사고력'. Don't mix it up with the same-sounding '사고' (accident).

examples.en: That school's diploma is recognized abroad too.
My effort was recognized, so I got an award.

examples.ko: 이번 결과는 실력으로 인정될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This result can be accepted as skill.
Without an ID, you won't be accepted as the person in question.
Write only the acknowledged facts in the article.
That singer was recognized overseas first.

explain: '인정하다'는 내가 받아들이는 것이고, '인정되다'는 다른 사람이나 제도가 그렇다고 봐 준다는 뜻이에요. '인정받다'는 더 자연스러운 말이라 '선생님께 인정받았어요'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: '인정하다' is when I accept something; '인정되다' is when others or a system accept it. '인정받다' is the more natural everyday choice, as in '선생님께 인정받았어요'.

examples.en: Grandmother is always warm toward her neighbors.

examples.ko: 인정스러운 주인 덕분에 밥을 공짜로 더 먹었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the kind owner, I got extra food for free.
That man helped us warmheartedly.
I like the village because the people are warm.
I still remember my kind-hearted teacher.
His words are rough, but he has a kind heart.

explain: '인정'은 사람을 아끼는 따뜻한 마음이고, '인정스럽다'는 그런 마음이 겉으로 보인다는 뜻이에요. '정이 많다', '따뜻하다'보다 조금 옛날 느낌이에요. 같은 소리의 '인정하다(accept)'와는 전혀 달라요.
explain_en: '인정' (human warmth) is a caring heart, and '인정스럽다' means it shows. It sounds a little more old-fashioned than '정이 많다' or '따뜻하다'. It is unrelated to '인정하다' (to accept).

examples.en: I skipped breakfast, so I'm very hungry.
If you're hungry, please eat first.
It's past lunchtime, so I'm a bit hungry.
I served warm soup to the hungry guest.
He must have been really hungry; he ate in no time.

examples.ko: 시장할 때 먹는 밥이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: Rice eaten when you're hungry tastes best.

explain: '배고프다'가 보통 말이고, '시장하다'는 조금 점잖고 공손한 말이에요. 어른께 '시장하시지요?'처럼 물을 때 써요. 같은 소리의 '시장(market)'과는 관계가 없어요.
explain_en: '배고프다' is the normal word; '시장하다' is more polite and refined. You'd ask an elder '시장하시지요?'. It has nothing to do with '시장' (market).

examples.en: The old part was replaced with a new one.
Could paper books be replaced by e-books?
People's work is being replaced by machines.
The substitute menu is the same price.

examples.ko: 이 약은 다른 약으로 대체되지 않아요.
examples.en: This medicine can't be substituted with another.
If sugar is replaced by honey, the taste changes.

explain: '바뀌다'는 단순히 달라진다는 뜻이고, '대체되다'는 원래 있던 것이 다른 것으로 자리를 내준다는 뜻이에요. 'A가 B로 대체되다'처럼 '~로'를 써요. 능동은 '대체하다'예요.
explain_en: '바뀌다' just means something changes; '대체되다' means something gives its place to another. Use '~로': 'A가 B로 대체되다'. The active form is '대체하다'.

examples.en: The Olympics are held every four years.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 큰 음악회가 개최될 예정이에요.
examples.en: A big concert is scheduled to be held next month.
The meeting was held in Seoul.
A thousand people came to the event that was held.
If it rains, the event won't be held.
I'm waiting for the day the festival is held.

explain: 큰 행사·대회·회의가 열릴 때 쓰는 공식적인 말이에요. 작은 모임에는 '열리다'를 써요. 파티가 '개최되다'라고 하면 너무 거창해요. 주최하는 쪽은 '개최하다'예요.
explain_en: A formal word for big events, contests and conferences. For small gatherings use '열리다'; saying a party is '개최되다' sounds grand. The organizer side is '개최하다'.

examples.en: This car is produced in Korea.
Rice is produced most in autumn.

examples.ko: 새 휴대폰이 다음 달부터 생산될 거예요.
examples.en: The new phone will be produced starting next month.
The products made go straight to the airport.

examples.ko: 이 지역에서는 사과가 많이 생산되고 있어요.
examples.en: Many apples are grown in this region.
The factory stopped, so goods couldn't be produced.

explain: 공장에서 만들든 농장에서 키우든 '생산되다'를 써요. 짝말은 '소비하다(consume)'예요. 집에서 만드는 음식에는 쓰지 않고 '만들어지다'를 써요.
explain_en: Whether made in a factory or grown on a farm, use '생산되다'. Its counterpart is '소비하다' (consume). For food made at home, use '만들어지다' instead.

examples.en: This job requires a lot of experience.
It is a situation that demands quick judgment.
Diligence is expected of new employees.
I submitted all the required documents.
In society, responsibility is often demanded.
That kind of behavior was not required.

explain: '필요하다'보다 강하게 '꼭 있어야 한다'고 요구받는 느낌이에요. 'A에게 B가 요구되다'처럼 주로 능력·자격·태도에 써요. 직접 요구할 때는 '요구하다', 부탁할 때는 '요청하다'가 더 부드러워요.
explain_en: Stronger than '필요하다': it feels like something is demanded of someone, usually skills, qualifications or attitude, as in 'A에게 B가 요구되다'. For making a demand yourself use '요구하다'; '요청하다' is softer.

en: be considered; be taken into account

examples.en: Students' opinions need to be taken into account.
The schedule changed because the weather was also considered.
Age isn't taken into account.

examples.ko: 고려된 방법 중에 이게 제일 싸요.
examples.en: Of the options considered, this is the cheapest.

examples.ko: 모든 사정이 고려되면 결과가 달라질 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If every circumstance is considered, the result may change.

examples.ko: 그 문제는 다음 계획에서 고려될 거예요.
examples.en: That issue will be considered in the next plan.

explain: '생각하다'보다 여러 조건을 따져 본다는 느낌의 말이에요. '고려하다'는 내가 따지는 것이고 '고려되다'는 결정 과정에서 반영된다는 뜻이에요. 소리가 비슷한 '배려'는 남의 처지를 생각해 마음 쓰는 것이라 달라요.
explain_en: Feels like weighing several conditions, more than '생각하다'. '고려하다' is you weighing; '고려되다' is something being reflected in a decision. Don't confuse it with '배려' (caring about someone's situation), which is a different word.

examples.en: My essay was selected as the best entry.
I'm glad I was chosen employee of the month.

examples.ko: 후보 중에서 한 명이 선정될 거예요.
examples.en: One of the candidates will be selected.
We text the people who were selected.
It was chosen as this year's best movie.
I'm sorry I wasn't selected in the review.

explain: '뽑히다'는 입말, '선정되다'는 심사나 기준을 거쳐 공식적으로 뽑힌다는 느낌이에요. 공모전·장학금·상 이야기에 자주 나와요. 고르는 쪽은 '선정하다'예요.
explain_en: '뽑히다' is spoken style; '선정되다' implies being chosen officially after a review or criteria. Common for contests, scholarships and awards. The choosing side is '선정하다'.

examples.ko: 회사가 다음 주에 새 앱을 출시해요.
examples.en: The company launches a new app next week.
That game was released last year.
The line was long on the day the new product launched.

examples.ko: 싼 모델을 출시하면 많이 팔릴 거예요.
examples.en: If they release a cheaper model, it will sell a lot.

examples.ko: 출시하기 전에 여러 번 시험해 봤어요.
examples.en: We tested it many times before releasing it.
We plan to release the new items in time for spring.

explain: 만든 물건을 처음 시장에 내놓을 때 써요. 영화·책에는 보통 '개봉하다'나 '출간하다'를 써요. 나온 물건이 주어이면 '출시되다'를 써요. 말로는 '나오다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Used when a product first goes on the market. For movies and books, people usually say '개봉하다' or '출간하다'. When the product is the subject, use '출시되다'. In speech, '나오다' is more natural.

examples.en: For a right to be exercised, certain conditions are needed.
The people's rights are being exercised properly.
The day the right to vote is exercised is coming.

examples.ko: 그 힘은 함부로 행사되면 안 돼요.
examples.en: That power must not be exercised carelessly.
The influence that was exerted was too big.
The authority couldn't be exercised, so the work was delayed.

explain: 주로 '권리·권한·영향력이 행사되다'처럼 법이나 제도 이야기에서만 써요. 소리가 같은 '행사(event)'와 달라요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고, 능동형 '행사하다'(권리를 행사하다)가 더 많아요.
explain_en: Mostly used in law and institutions: '권리·권한·영향력이 행사되다'. It is different from '행사' (event). Rare in daily talk; the active '행사하다' (exercise a right) is more common.

examples.en: An expert appraised this painting for me.
They appraised the ring at the jewelry shop.
You need a lot of experience to appraise antiques.
The appraised price was higher than I expected.
I'd like to have grandmother's watch appraised.
It takes a week to determine whether it's real.

explain: 물건의 값이나 진짜·가짜를 전문가가 따져 보는 일이에요. 같은 소리의 '감정(feeling)'과는 전혀 달라요. 주로 '감정을 받다', '감정을 맡기다'로 쓰고, 가게에서는 '감정해 주세요'라고 부탁해요.
explain_en: An expert determines an object's value or authenticity. It is unrelated to the same-sounding '감정' (feeling). Commonly '감정을 받다' or '감정을 맡기다'; at a shop you ask '감정해 주세요'.

examples.en: A big bridge is being built here.
A new airport was built on the coast.
A park will be built in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 건설된 지 오십 년이 된 건물이에요.
examples.en: It's a building that was built fifty years ago.
When the road is built, travel time gets shorter.
It's a city built by cutting into mountains.

explain: '짓다'는 집·건물에 쓰고, '건설되다'는 다리·도로·댐·도시처럼 큰 시설에 써요. '건설되다'는 집에는 어색해요. '세워지다'도 건물이나 기념비에 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '짓다' is for houses and buildings; '건설되다' is for large structures like bridges, roads, dams and cities. It sounds off for a house. '세워지다' also works for buildings and monuments.

examples.en: That rumor was denied by the company.

examples.ko: 그 보도 내용은 관계자에 의해 부인되었어요.
examples.en: The content of that report was denied by an official.
The connection to that incident was denied to the end.
I'll take out the denied content from the article.
The contract's validity might be denied.
The facts weren't denied and were accepted.

explain: '부인되다'는 어떤 주장이 사실이 아니라고 거부당한다는 뜻이고, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. '부인(否認, deny)'과 '부인(婦人, wife)'은 한자와 뜻이 완전히 달라요. 반대말은 '인정되다'예요.
explain_en: '부인되다' means a claim is rejected as untrue and shows up often in the news. '부인' (deny) and '부인' (a married woman) are different words with different Chinese characters. The opposite is '인정되다'.

en: be undercooked; be half-ripe; be unripe

examples.en: The rice is undercooked and hard to eat.
The potatoes weren't cooked enough, so they were underdone.
Half-ripe fruit tastes underdone.
If the meat is undercooked, I'll grill it again.
The noodles are fine even if they're a bit underdone.
I cooked the undercooked rice again.

explain: 음식이 덜 익은 상태를 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '덜 익다'도 쓰는데, '설다'는 주로 밥이나 과일에 써요. 'ㄹ' 받침이라 '선 밥'처럼 변해요. '설익다'는 비슷하지만 따로 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: Describes food that isn't fully cooked. '덜 익다' means the same, but '설다' is mostly for rice and fruit. The ㄹ stem changes as in '선 밥'. '설익다' is a similar but separate word.

examples.ko: 알람이 아침 일곱 시로 설정돼 있어요.
examples.en: The alarm is set for seven in the morning.
A new password has been set.
If the goal is set too high, it's hard.
After the set time passes, the screen turns off.
The language is set to Korean.
The price is expected to be set low.

explain: 휴대폰·프로그램의 '설정'은 값을 정해 두는 일이고, '설정되다'는 이미 그렇게 정해진 상태예요. 목표·기준에도 써요. 말로는 '맞춰져 있다'가 더 자연스럽고, 직접 바꿀 때는 '설정하다'를 써요.
explain_en: For phones and programs, '설정' is fixing a value; '설정되다' means it is already set. It also works for goals and standards. In speech, '맞춰져 있다' is more natural; when you change it yourself, use '설정하다'.

examples.en: A new system will be implemented from next week.
The exam was carried out nationwide at the same time.
This test is carried out every year.
The results of the survey that was conducted were announced.
It's the period when free checkups are offered.
The inspection couldn't be carried out because of the rain.

explain: '하다'의 공식적인 말로, 조사·시험·제도·검사처럼 계획된 일이 실제로 시작될 때 써요. '시행되다'는 법과 제도가 효력을 가질 때, '실시되다'는 조사·시험 같은 행동이 이뤄질 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '하다'를 써요.
explain_en: A formal version of '하다' for planned things like surveys, exams, systems and inspections actually being carried out. '시행되다' is for laws and rules taking effect; '실시되다' for actions like surveys and tests. In daily talk, people just say '하다'.

examples.en: Our company is located in Gangnam, Seoul.
That university is located in Busan.
I moved to the city where the head office is located.
The area where the factory is located is quiet.
Do you know where the post office is located?
The hospital is near the station, so it's convenient.

explain: 주소·위치를 공식적으로 말할 때 '~에 소재하다'로 써요. 말로는 '있다'나 '위치하다'가 더 자연스럽고, 서류·뉴스에서는 '소재지'(회사나 기관이 있는 곳)로 자주 봐요. 사람이 있는 곳에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Used officially for an address or location: '~에 소재하다'. In speech, '있다' or '위치하다' is more natural; in documents and news you often see '소재지' (where a company or office is located). It isn't used for where a person is.

examples.ko: 이 행사는 여름 방학에 맞춰 기획됐어요.
examples.en: This event was planned to fit the summer break.
A new program is being planned for the students.
It changed a lot from what was first planned.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 십 년 전에 기획되었어요.
examples.en: That movie was planned ten years ago.
It took a long time for the exhibition to be planned.

examples.ko: 새 상품이 기획되는 과정을 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to see how a new product gets planned.

explain: '계획'은 앞으로 할 일의 순서를 정하는 것이고, '기획'은 새로운 것을 생각해 내서 짜 놓는 거예요. 영화·방송·전시·상품에 많이 써요. 개인의 하루 일정에는 '계획'을 써요.
explain_en: '계획' is deciding steps for what to do; '기획' is coming up with something new and putting it together. Common for movies, TV, exhibitions and products. For a personal daily schedule, use '계획'.

examples.en: After I took the medicine, my cough calmed down.
Let's talk again once you've calmed down.
The protest settled down as night came.
We started the meeting in a calmer atmosphere.
Prices seem likely to settle soon.
When the child is held, the crying settles.

explain: '진정하다'는 내가 마음을 가라앉히는 것이고, '진정되다'는 흥분·통증·소란이 저절로 가라앉는 것이에요. '진정하세요'는 '진정하다'의 명령이라 흥분한 사람에게 해요. '진정되다'는 사람에게 명령하지 않아요.
explain_en: '진정하다' is you calming yourself; '진정되다' is excitement, pain or commotion subsiding on its own. '진정하세요' (calm down!) comes from '진정하다'; you don't give commands with '진정되다'.
